# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 79 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 79 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_079_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 2

**1** Among these the angel commanded that crowns be brought; palm-branch crowns were brought, and the angel crowned those men who had given back completely green rods and sent them into the tower. **2** He also sent into the tower those whose rods were green but cracked, giving them seals. **3** All who went into the tower wore the same garment — white as snow. **4** He also sent away those who had returned rods half-green and half-withered, giving them clothing and seals. **5** As for those who gave back rods that were withered and moth-eaten — their status was that of apostates, of those who had betrayed the church and blasphemed the Lord through their shameful deeds; moreover, they were ashamed of the name of the Lord by which they had been called. These therefore perished utterly. **6** Those whose rods were withered but not moth-eaten — these were hearers of the word who remained in their sins without repenting. Those who returned rods half-green and half-withered — these are people occupied with business who do not attach themselves to the saints; therefore half of them is living and half is dead. **7** Those who brought rods two-thirds green and one-third withered are those who denied the faith; they denied it many times. **8** Those who returned rods two-thirds withered and one-third green — these are men who believed, but for the most part they have lived in iniquity and wickedness, though some portion of righteousness remains in them. **9** Those who returned nearly all green rods with only the tip withered — these are those who believed truly and are faithful, but carry slight blemishes. **10** And those who returned completely withered rods — these are those who have already apostatized and do not repent, nor will they repent on account of the hardness of their hearts; therefore the spirit of the Lord departed from them.

---

*LOGOS formally preserves the systematic interpretation. "Apostates" renders the Greek apostátai. The tower represents the Church; the seals likely represent baptism.*
